items.title: John L. Jones Interview, 1972-06-05
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] You know him, Nick? Yeah, I've heard of him because I interviewed John.

ctx.x: And he had a drummer by the name of Albert Jow. You heard of him? Oh yeah. I knew him. Then we had all the way through, we had uh, uh, Poirier, Allison Poirier on piano. He stayed with Isaiah Morgan. And when I left Morgan, I joined the John Casimir band. The John Casimir, I started playing at Claiborne and Tulane Avenue. John had a man playing trumpet, he alternated by the name of Wooden Joe. Oh yeah. Uh huh. And that's who else John had. John had, I can't, I don't know the rest of this man's name. He had…
Juniors? Never heard of him. You know him, Nick? Yeah, I've heard of him because I interviewed John.

And then later on, Wooden Joe left, John got Louis Dumain. And when I left, that's when this man came and played the drum. What is his name? Uh, Matthews. That's the only band I ever know from the place. Fat, Fat, Fat Houston. Fat Houston started on the drum. He was, he started then on the drum. Matthew Houston. Matthew Houston. He started playing with John. I didn't know where to play with him. After I left John. And then John broke that band up and we come back and we start playing at the Rose Club. Mandeville…
